summary: The main article describes a metal-free photoredox intramolecular cyclization of N-aryl acrylamides using 4CzIPN and decanal to produce oxindoles. It includes optimization tables, substrate scope figures, and mechanistic schemes, while the characterization section provides detailed data for 22 specific products.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: Bioactive molecules containing the oxindole motif.
items.description: Displays the chemical structures of bioactive drugs like Ubrogepant and Rhynchophylline that contain the oxindole core.

items.heading: Figure 2
items.caption: Cyclization and hydroarylation methods.
items.description: Compares previous methods for hydroarylation and cyclization with the current work's metal-free photoredox approach.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of Reaction Conditions a .
items.description: Lists the screening of photocatalysts, additives, and solvents to determine the optimal conditions for the cyclization of 1a to 2a.

items.heading: Figure 3
items.caption: Substrate scope of photocyclization of N -arylacrylamides.
items.description: Shows the variety of N-arylacrylamides that successfully underwent cyclization to form functionalized oxindoles with their respective yields.

items.heading: Figure 4
items.caption: Competitive cyclization.
items.description: Illustrates the site-selectivity control between 6-endo-trig and 5-exo-trig cyclization based on the amount of decanal used.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Mechanistic studies.
items.description: Presents radical inhibition, H/D exchange, and Stern-Volmer quenching experiments to elucidate the reaction mechanism.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Possible reaction mechanism.
items.description: Proposes a consecutive photoinduced electron transfer (ConPET) pathway for the cyclization reaction.
